Let
\[
d=\gcd(m,n).
\]
Then the genus is
\[
\boxed{
g(C)=
\begin{cases}
1+mn-\dfrac{m+n+2d}{2}, & m,n\text{ both odd},\\[6pt]
1+mn-\dfrac{m+n+3d}{2}, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}}
\]

**Solution.**  
Let \(F=\mathbb C(x)\), \(a=x(x-1)\), \(b=x(x-\lambda)\), and
\[
L=F(y,z),\qquad y^m=a,\quad z^n=b.
\]
Since \(a\) has valuation \(1\) at \(x=1\), it is not a nontrivial power in \(F\), so \([F(y):F]=m\). Over \(F(y)\), every place above \(x=\lambda\) is unramified in \(F(y)/F\), because \(v_\lambda(a)=0\), while \(v_\lambda(b)=1\). Hence \(b\) is not a nontrivial \(q\)-th power in \(F(y)\) for any prime \(q\mid n\), so
\[
[L:F]=mn.
\]
Thus \(C\to \mathbb P^1_x\) is a Galois cover of degree \(mn\).

The only possible branch points are
\[
x=0,\ 1,\ \lambda,\ \infty.
\]
Locally, the ramification index is the order of the subgroup of \(\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\) generated by the relevant valuations divided by \(m,n\).

At \(x=0\), the valuations of \(a,b\) are both \(1\), so
\[
e_0=\operatorname{lcm}(m,n).
\]
At \(x=1\),
\[
e_1=m,
\]
and at \(x=\lambda\),
\[
e_\lambda=n.
\]
At infinity, both \(a,b\) have valuation \(-2\), so
\[
e_\infty=\frac{\operatorname{lcm}(m,n)}{\gcd(\operatorname{lcm}(m,n),2)}.
\]

By Riemann-Hurwitz,
\[
2g(C)-2
=
-2mn
+
mn\left[
\left(1-\frac1{e_0}\right)
+\left(1-\frac1m\right)
+\left(1-\frac1n\right)
+\left(1-\frac1{e_\infty}\right)
\right].
\]
So
\[
g(C)
=
1+\frac{mn}{2}
\left(
2-\frac1m-\frac1n-\frac1{\operatorname{lcm}(m,n)}-\frac1{e_\infty}
\right).
\]
Since
\[
\frac{mn}{\operatorname{lcm}(m,n)}=d,
\]
and
\[
\frac{mn}{e_\infty}
=
\begin{cases}
d, & m,n\text{ both odd},\\
2d, & \text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]
we get
\[
g(C)=
\begin{cases}
1+mn-\dfrac{m+n+2d}{2}, & m,n\text{ both odd},\\[6pt]
1+mn-\dfrac{m+n+3d}{2}, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

Final answer:
\[
\boxed{
\begin{cases}
1+mn-\dfrac{m+n+2\gcd(m,n)}{2}, & m,n\text{ both odd},\\[6pt]
1+mn-\dfrac{m+n+3\gcd(m,n)}{2}, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}}
\]
